Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision during a lane change, reporting neck
and low back pain with associated stiffness and headaches. The mechanism of injury is
consistent in type and force with the symptoms described. Initial examination showed
reduced cerviacl and lumbar range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness,
supporting a soft tissue strain of the neck and back. Other neurological and
orthopedic screening tests were within normal limits. No prior injury to the cervical
or lumbar spine is documented in the available history. Care has included 43 visits to
date, consisting of chiropractic manipulation, physical therapy, and soft tissue
treatment. Over time, the frequency of visits and the number of added service types
have increased steadily beyond what is typically expected for a strain of this
severity, and the reasons for this escalation are not fully explained in the record.
Billing review found no duplicate or repeated charges for the same services.
Recommendation is to reassess functional progress and establish a defined discharge
plan with clear goals.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page

- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
